title: Anyone else notice their LLM review is brilliant at explaining losses but teaches you nothing?
author: CryptographerBig7624
selftext:
I had a setup where at the end of each day i handed my trade history to an llm and asked it to review the session. and it was great, clean confident explanations for why every trade worked or didn't. took me too long to notice the explanations were basically fiction. give a model a list of trades and it'll happily generate a compelling story for each one, in hindsight, after the outcome is already known.

the tell was that the lessons never improved anything. i was building a very articulate feedback loop that taught me nothing, because a hindsight narrative isn't a hypothesis, it's just a story that fits data it already saw.

what fixed it was changing the ask. now the review's only job is to produce one falsifiable hypothesis i can test separately on data it hasn't seen. if it can't be measured and proven wrong, it doesn't count.

so for anyone using an llm in their review loop, how do you keep it honest? do you let it explain trades, or do you force it into something testable? genuinely want to compare approaches because i suspect a lot of us are getting confidently narrated nonsense and calling it analysis
